STATE OF WASHINGTON
Office of the Governor
PLANNING AND COMMUNITY AFFAIRS AGENCY
OLYMPIA, WASHINGTON 98504
July 18, 1972
Mr. G. Douglas Hofe, Jr.
Director
Bureau of Outdoor Recreation
United States Department of the Interior
Washington, D. C. 20240
Dear Mr. Hofe:
RE: K-14
Pursuant to the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969, following are my comments relating to your draft Environmental Impact Statement on off-road vehicles (ORV) on public lands.
From a state perspective, I recommend that copies of this draft be circulated among primary state land management and regulatory agencies. These would include the Departments of Highways, Natural Resources, Fisheries, Game, Ecology, Parks and Recreation, and Social and Health Services.
It appears that the main consideration regarding ORV use is a flexible use criteria, (pages 2-31). According to the draft, this will be the responsibility of each respective land manager at the federal level to assure that the scenic, natural and aesthetic order is maintained. I realize the difficulty of uniform regulations for the entire Department of Interior because of the many variables one must consider for lands that range from mountains to desert to wetlands.
In the course of policy development, I suggest coordination with local units of governments, particularly at the county level (county commissioners) in order to apprise them of your efforts. This could precipitate ORV policies at the county level.
These are my primary comments at this time. Thank you for the opportunity to comment.
Sincerely yours,
Richard H. Slavin
Director
